data.body:
Deadlock fixed and shipped: change 1028, merged 5644a0d7b39494ea0e4a6ef0f6918c98d4ab6f32.

CORRECTION to my earlier comments on this ticket. I twice claimed experiment had refuted the review finding that run_repair self-deadlocks. Both claims were wrong and are withdrawn. The probes ran against the synthetic graph-test tracker, which is NOT a git repo, so stage_and_commit bails before it ever takes the write lock and rev-parse HEAD returns empty — every assertion compared "" to "" and passed vacuously. The probe could not have detected a deadlock whether or not one existed.

Re-run against a REAL git-backed tracker, the result is unambiguous:
- repair_finding with no outer lock -> repair_status=repaired in 0.1s
- run_repair (outer lock held)      -> repair_status=unrepairable in 60.0s, CommandError: flock: could not acquire lock after 60s

The review finding was correct. run_repair held the tracker write lock across its loop; every inner write takes that same non-re-entrant lock via append_event -> write_and_push -> stage_and_commit -> write_lock, blocked on the lock its own process held, burned the full 60s timeout and failed. 18 findings x 60s explains the observed zero-progress-in-ten-minutes exactly.

Fix: drop the outer lock. Repair needs no cross-item atomicity — the replacement link is written before the stale unlink, so an interruption leaves a superset the next run converges. The pre-repair tag and the reconciler in-flight guard are unchanged; neither needs the store write lock.

Tests added, including the two this ticket AC named and I had never written — which is what surfaced the defect, via the completion verifier refusing to close on unmet criteria:
- test_run_repair_does_not_hold_a_lock_that_blocks_its_own_writes — asserts repaired, no flock in the reason, and elapsed < 30s. Mutation-checked: restoring the outer lock turns it RED in 60.4s.
- test_repair_force_writes_the_pre_repair_tag_and_repoints_it — builds a real git-backed tracker (documented in the test, since that fixture gap is what hid the bug) and asserts a second run RE-POINTS the tag. Earlier drafts of this test were tautological twice over: HEAD never moved between runs, and rev-parse of an absent tag echoes the ref name rather than empty. Both corrected.
- test_link_audit_arm_reconverges_only_for_repair — init_only=True without --repair, False with. Mutation-checked.

Live verification of the shipped command (no workaround driver): `rebar link-audit --repair --output json` against this repository tracker now runs to completion, writes pre-link-audit-repair @ 0c4154e3a453, and reports 8 findings all repair_status=unrepairable with the closed-source reason. Exit 1 because findings remain. Previously this command hung for 10 minutes and repaired nothing.

Store state unchanged by that run (all 8 are the known closed-endpoint residuals). Cumulative remediation across this ticket: 12 edges repaired, 8 inert residuals, 0 scheduling-affecting.
